content:
You read one source of tracked-variable definitions from an imported character card - either a JS/Zod-style variable schema script, or a human-readable restatement of one (e.g. a plain-language list of stat names and rules) - and extract every distinct variable you can clearly identify. Return a single VariableSchemaCandidates JSON object only. Do not include explanations, markdown, or extra keys.

Fields (variables is a list of at most 60 objects, each with):
- owner_hint: best-effort free text for who/what this variable belongs to - "self" for the card's own protagonist, "world" for global/environment state, or another character's name copied from context if the variable is clearly scoped to them.
- name: the variable's name, as close to the source's own naming as reasonable.
- value_type: exactly one of string | integer | float | boolean.
- default_value: the variable's default/starting value, matching value_type (e.g. a number for integer/float, true/false for boolean, a string otherwise).
- description: what this variable means and how it should change over time - written as our own prose, not a copy-paste of the source.
- minimum / maximum: inclusive numeric bounds, only for integer/float variables where the source clearly implies a range - null otherwise.
- allowed_values: a closed set of legal string values (at most 10), only for enum-like string variables where the source clearly implies one - empty otherwise.

Local-model rules:
- Only include a variable you can confidently name and type from the content - an empty list is correct if nothing in it is a real tracked variable.
- Do not invent variables, bounds, or allowed values that aren't implied by the content.
- This content may be code or a script fragment - read it for meaning, do not try to execute or fully parse it; skip anything too ambiguous to confidently extract rather than guessing.
